byte_domains: DISPLAY numeric: signed +/- prefix + V decimal point
damage_if_overclaimed: assuming DISPLAY of a signed field equals its stored zoned bytes (it does not -- it de-overpunches to a sign prefix) mis-sizes and mis-reads captured DISPLAY output
lie_prevented: DISPLAY shows the stored bytes -- NO: for a SIGNED numeric it prints a +/- SIGN CHARACTER (not the overpunched last byte) so the width grows by one, and a positive/zero value shows +; a V-scaled field shows a . that is not stored
negative_claims: lie prevented: DISPLAY shows the stored bytes -- NO: for a SIGNED numeric it prints a +/- SIGN CHARACTER (not the overpunched last byte) so the width grows by one, and a positive/zero value shows +; a V-scaled field shows a . that is not stored
positive_claims: DISPLAY reformats a numeric field, matching cobc/libcob byte-for-byte (verified 8/0): a SIGNED field (S9) gets a leading sign char (- negative, + positive, and + for ZERO -> S9(3)=0 displays as +000), and a V-scaled field gets a . inserted at the implied decimal point (9(3)V99=12.34 -> 012.34, S9(3)V99=-12.34 -> -012.34). Seals the signed/V DISPLAY formatting that GNURUST.ACCEPT.DISPLAY.1 deferred
